budget_items.what_was_said: The signed FY27 state budget included additional education-specific receipts beyond what the town's budget assumed, largely through charter school reimbursement rather than Chapter 70, so it is not guaranteed to recur.

budget_items.topic: Proposed FY27 warrant article for schools
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee discussed a warrant article asking the town to raise and appropriate an additional sum for the FY27 school operating budget, to go before the Select Board and a November special town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Gap between state receipts and town-supported school spending
budget_items.what_was_said: Mandy said the town manager and Select Board will only support spending $350,000 of the new state money on schools this year, leaving a gap she said the town is keeping rather than passing to the district.
Proposed 1.0 reading specialist for the primary school, funded from health-insurance premium savings rather than the new state money.
Proposed using this amount from the new legislative funding to fund a reading specialist position at Turkey Hill Elementary.
Dr. Fortuna recommended increasing the advertised 0.5 assistant principal position to a full 1.0 position at the high school, citing lack of candidates and culture/climate survey data.
Proposed funding for additional online one-to-one tutoring seats at this cost, noting seats can be reassigned as students meet goals so more students than the seat count could be served.
Proposed increasing the current 0.6 music teacher position by 0.4 to a full 1.0, which would also let the teacher cover an extra wellness section to relieve high school scheduling bottlenecks.

budget_items.topic: Which spending items are considered fully funded
budget_items.what_was_said: Chris reportedly feels confident health insurance savings and end-of-year supply purchasing can cover the Turkey Hill reading specialist and the assistant principal, but not the Ignite seats or the 0.4 music teacher increase without continued austere budget management.
Transfers, along with warrants and donations, were noted as not ready this meeting and pushed to the next meeting.

budget_items.topic: Possible per-student state reimbursement to towns
budget_items.what_was_said: Reference to news that Governor Healey may be looking at a per-student reimbursement basis to towns; details were garbled and described as possibly still in the works.

decisions.decision: Line item transfers, warrants, and donations were deferred to the next meeting.
The custodial union MOU was not voted on because the custodial union had not yet seen it; the chair said it would come back around July 29th.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee met to consider a warrant article seeking an additional $350,000 for the FY27 school budget, funded from new state education receipts, and a related spending plan (reading specialists, an expanded assistant principal position, tutoring seats, and a music teacher increase). After extended, often heated debate about whether to push for a special town meeting sooner versus accepting the town manager/Select Board's proposed timeline, the committee approved the spending plan and voted on the warrant article (outcome of that final roll call not fully audible in the captions), while transfers and a custodial union MOU were deferred to future meetings.
